notes.md: - **Three-language formula:** recommended by the **Kothari Commission (1964-66)** and adopted in the **National Policy on Education, 1968**. **NEP 2020** keeps it with flexibility: at least **two of the three languages native to India**; no language is imposed on any State.
- **World Urbanization Prospects 2025 (UN DESA, Nov 2025):** **33 megacities** in 2025 (8 in 1975), **37** by 2050; **two-thirds** of world population growth to 2050 projected in cities.

new.s: In racial classification by hair form, which group has woolly hair, described as ulotrichi?
new.x: Ulotrichi (woolly) hair marks the Negroid group; leiotrichi is straight (Mongoloid) and cymotrichi is wavy (Caucasoid).
new.angle: U0655 notes gap: ulotrichi hair -> Negroid

new.s: In B.S. Guha's classification, traces of which racial element are found among the Kadar and Irula tribes?
new.x: Guha placed the Andaman tribes under Negrito and noted Negrito traces among the Kadar and Irula of south India.
new.angle: U0655 notes gap: Kadar, Irula -> Negrito traces

new.s: In which year did the Anthropological Survey of India move its headquarters to Kolkata?
new.x: The AnSI was founded at Varanasi in 1945 and moved to Kolkata, its headquarters, in 1948.
new.angle: U0655 notes gap: AnSI moved to Kolkata 1948

new.s: Which State has the highest share of Buddhists in its population, as per Census 2011?
new.x: Sikkim (then Arunachal Pradesh) has the highest Buddhist share, while Maharashtra has the largest number of Buddhists.
new.angle: U0656 notes gap: Buddhist highest share -> Sikkim

new.s: In which State were Muslims in a majority, at about 68% of the population, in Census 2011?
new.x: Muslims formed about 68% of the population of Jammu and Kashmir; Lakshadweep (about 97%) is the UT with a Muslim majority.
new.angle: U0656 notes gap: Muslim majority State -> J&K

new.s: What was the decadal growth rate of the Hindu population during 2001-11?
new.x: Hindus grew by 16.8% in 2001-11; 24.6% was the Muslim rate, 15.5% the Christian and 8.4% the Sikh rate.
new.angle: U0656 notes gap: Hindu growth rate 16.8%

new.s: What is the name of the portal on which waqf property data must be uploaded under the Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025?
new.x: The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2025, in force from 8 April 2025, requires waqf property data on the UMEED portal.
new.angle: U0656 notes gap: Waqf Amendment Act 2025 -> UMEED portal

new.s: Which language was declared a classical language of India in 2014?
new.x: Odia became a classical language in 2014; Malayalam was declared in 2013 and Kannada in 2008.
new.angle: U0657 notes gap: Odia classical 2014

new.s: Which was the second language to be declared a classical language of India, in 2005?
new.x: Tamil was first (2004), Sanskrit second (2005), and Telugu and Kannada followed in 2008.
new.angle: U0657 notes gap: Sanskrit classical 2005

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution provides for an Official Language Commission appointed by the President?
new.x: Article 344 provides for the President's Official Language Commission and a Parliamentary Committee.
new.angle: U0657 notes gap: Art 344 -> Official Language Commission

new.s: Where was the office of the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities, set up under Article 350B in 1957, located?
new.x: The Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities was appointed in 1957 with the office at Allahabad.
new.angle: U0657 notes gap: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities -> 1957, Allahabad

new.s: Hindi Diwas is observed on 14 September to mark the adoption of which of the following?
new.x: On 14 September 1949 the Constituent Assembly adopted the Munshi-Ayyangar formula on Hindi in Devanagari; the day is Hindi Diwas.
new.angle: U0657 notes gap: Hindi Diwas 14 Sep -> Munshi-Ayyangar formula

new.s: Which of the following is an official language of Sikkim?
new.x: Sikkim's official languages include Nepali, Sikkimese (Bhutia), Lepcha and English.
new.angle: U0657 #6 notes gap: Sikkim -> official languages

new.s: Gondi, a tribal language of central India, belongs to which language family?
new.x: Gondi, like Kui and Kurukh, belongs to the Central/North branch of the Dravidian family.
new.angle: U0657 notes gap: Gondi -> Dravidian

new.s: Nicobarese belongs to which branch of the Austro-Asiatic language family?
new.x: Khasi and Nicobarese are Mon-Khmer languages of the Austro-Asiatic family; Santhali and Mundari are Munda.
new.angle: U0657 notes gap: Nicobarese -> Mon-Khmer

new.s: With which movement is Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy, whose birth anniversary is Telugu Language Day, associated?
new.x: Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy led the Vyavaharika Telugu movement for spoken Telugu and prepared script and dictionaries for Savara.
new.angle: U0657 notes gap: Gidugu -> Vyavaharika Telugu

new.s: In which policy was the three-language formula formally adopted?
new.x: The three-language formula, recommended by the Kothari Commission (1964-66), was adopted in the National Policy on Education, 1968.
new.angle: U0657 #7 web: three-language formula -> NPE 1968

new.s: Under the National Education Policy 2020, how many of the three languages in the three-language formula must be native to India?
new.x: NEP 2020 keeps the formula with flexibility: States and students choose, so long as at least two of the three languages are native to India, and no language is imposed.
new.angle: U0657 #7 web: NEP 2020 three-language formula

new.s: According to PLFS 2020-21, what was the migration rate among females in India?
new.x: PLFS 2020-21 put the female migration rate at 47.9% (86.8% of them for marriage); the male rate was 10.7%.
new.angle: U0658 notes gap: female migration rate 47.9%

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Under Article 243P, a metropolitan area has a population of 10 lakh or more.
2. A mega city has a population of 10 million or more.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Article 243P defines a metropolitan area as 10 lakh or more people; a mega city has 10 million (1 crore) or more.
new.angle: U0659 #15 notes gap: Art 243P metropolitan area; mega city threshold

new.s: Which Article of the Constitution defines a 'metropolitan area'?
new.x: Article 243P (Part IXA, 74th Amendment) defines a metropolitan area as one with 10 lakh or more people.
new.angle: U0659 #15 notes gap: Art 243P metropolitan area

new.s: What was India's urban population in Census 2011?
new.x: India's urban population rose from 286 million (2001) to 377.1 million (2011); 833.1 million was rural.
new.angle: U0659 #10 notes gap: urban population 2011 = 377.1 million

new.s: After Goa, which was the next most urbanised State in Census 2011?
new.x: Goa (62.17%) was the most urbanised State, followed by Mizoram, Tamil Nadu and Kerala.
new.angle: U0659 #11 notes gap: second most urbanised State -> Mizoram

new.s: Which State had the smallest urban population in Census 2011?
new.x: Sikkim had the smallest urban population (about 0.15 million), followed by Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram.
new.angle: U0659 #11 notes gap: smallest urban population -> Sikkim

new.s: In the functional classification of towns, Kandla and Kochi are examples of which type of town?
new.x: Kandla, Kochi and Visakhapatnam are port towns, classed as transport and trade towns.
new.angle: U0659 #13 notes gap: port towns -> Kandla, Kochi

new.s: Which of the following towns is of medieval origin?
new.x: Hyderabad, like Delhi, Jaipur, Lucknow and Agra, is a medieval town; Madurai is ancient and Chandigarh and Bhubaneswar are post-1947 planned towns.
new.angle: U0659 #13 notes gap: towns by historical origin -> Hyderabad medieval

new.s: In which year was the Chennai Metropolitan Development Authority (CMDA) set up?
new.x: CMDA was set up in 1974, after DDA (1957) and KMDA (1970) and before MMRDA (1975).
new.angle: U0659 #5 notes gap: CMDA 1974

new.s: When was Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban 2.0, aiming at 'Garbage Free' cities, launched?
new.x: SBM-U 2.0 was launched on 1 October 2021 to make cities 'Garbage Free', with an outlay of Rs 1.41 lakh crore.
new.angle: U0659 #14 notes gap: SBM-U 2.0 -> 1 Oct 2021, Garbage Free

new.s: According to the UN's World Urbanization Prospects 2025, how many megacities were there in the world in 2025?
new.x: WUP 2025 counts 33 megacities in 2025, up from 8 in 1975; 37 are projected by 2050.
new.angle: U0659 #10 web: global urban projections -> megacities count (WUP 2025)

new.s: Which organisation publishes the World Urbanization Prospects, whose 2025 edition says cities hold 45% of the world's population?
new.x: The World Urbanization Prospects is published by the UN Department of Economic and Social Affairs (UN DESA); its 2025 edition says 45% of 8.2 billion people live in cities.
new.angle: U0659 #10 web: global urban projections -> WUP publisher

new.s: In the UN lists of the world's largest cities before WUP 2025, which city was ranked first?
new.x: Earlier UN lists ranked Tokyo first and Delhi second; WUP 2025's new method puts Jakarta first.
new.angle: U0660 #3 notes gap: earlier UN lists -> Tokyo 1st (APPSC 2018 key)

new.s: According to the World Urbanization Prospects 2025, which city is the world's second most populous?
new.x: WUP 2025 ranks Jakarta first, Dhaka second, Tokyo third and New Delhi fourth.
new.angle: U0660 #3 notes gap: WUP 2025 -> Dhaka 2nd

new.s: According to the World Urbanization Prospects 2025, what share of the world's 8.2 billion people live in cities?
new.x: WUP 2025 says cities hold 45% of the world's 8.2 billion people.
new.angle: U0660 #3 notes gap: cities = 45% of world population (WUP 2025)

new.s: Which is the most polluted capital city in the world?
new.x: Delhi is the most polluted capital, and 8 of the world's 10 most polluted cities are in India.
new.angle: U0660 #5 notes gap: most polluted capital -> Delhi

new.s: Which city topped the Super Swachh League for cities of 3-10 lakh population in Swachh Survekshan 2024-25?
new.x: Noida led the 3-10 lakh Super Swachh League, followed by Chandigarh and Mysuru; Indore led the 10 lakh+ league.
new.angle: U0660 #9 notes gap: Super Swachh League 3-10 lakh -> Noida
